observation_summary: The DateTimeFormatter.parseInto method fails to correctly handle date parsing when the format string does not include a year, resulting in incorrect year values (e.g., defaulting to 2000 instead of the base year or the specified default year).
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the internal logic of the date parsing algorithm when a year is missing from the format. The formatter is not correctly applying the base year or the default year during the parsing process, which is a procedural error in how the date components are assembled. This is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error, but a flaw in the computational strategy for date reconstruction.
evidence_used: The bug report states 'DateTimeFormatter.parseInto broken when no year in format'.
Failing tests show incorrect year results (e.g., 2000 instead of 2004) when parsing month-only or month-day formats.
The stack traces point to failures in date parsing logic within the Joda-Time library.
evidence_gaps: The specific production code responsible for the parsing logic is not provided in the snippets, only the test code and abstract class definitions.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the result is an incorrect year value, the root cause is the procedural logic that fails to correctly calculate or assign the year based on the provided context, rather than a simple incorrect constant or variable initialization.
There is no evidence that a missing guard or condition is the primary cause; the logic itself is performing the wrong calculation for the year.
